Method of Attack: DNS cache poisoning via side-channel attack to deduce source port number
Exploitation of Kaminsky's DNS cache poisoning bug by guessing transaction IDs after deducing source port
Flooding DNS resolver with spoofed packets to random ports to deduce open ports using Linux ICMP rate limiter behavior
Discoverer: Researchers from Tsinghua University and the University of California
Impacted Systems: DNS resolvers such as BIND, Unbound, dnsmasq
Attack Vector: DNS cache poisoning via spoofed DNS responses
Side-channel attack exploiting Linux kernel ICMP rate limiter
Indicators of Compromise: Spoofed DNS responses with guessed transaction IDs
Malicious IP addresses returned in DNS cache (e.g., attacker-controlled IP instead of legitimate IP)
Example IP: 104.20.60.209 (legitimate bleepingcomputer.com IP used as reference)
